query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Systematic variation of the Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr elemental composition in the HfNbTaTiZr-HEA through controlled alloying will result in a change in the mechanical properties, such as yield strength and hardness, due to the alteration of the lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening mechanisms.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy with a uniform elemental composition
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of the elemental composition through controlled alloying, with a range of 5-20 at.% variation for each element
generation.conditions: Room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 800°C) under various mechanical testing conditions (e.g., tension, compression, hardness)
generation.mechanism: Alteration of the lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening mechanisms due to changes in the elemental composition
generation.predicted_outcome: A 10-20% change in yield strength and a 5-15% change in hardness relative to the baseline composition
generation.baseline: The mechanical properties of the HfNbTaTiZr-HEA with the initial uniform elemental composition
generation.boundary: The range of elemental composition variations (5-20 at.%) and the temperature range (up to 800°C)
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between the elemental composition and the mechanical properties is unknown, and the effects of other microstructural features, such as grain size and precipitates, may influence the results

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled variable experiment with systematic variation of the elemental composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the change in yield strength and hardness is less than 5% relative to the baseline composition for all elemental composition variations, the hypothesis is falsified

system.state: polycrystalline or single-crystal form with varying elemental compositions

frame.goal: understanding the effects of changing elemental percentages on mechanical properties
frame.limitation: individual constituents' effects on mechanical properties are unknown
root_cause_cues: individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored

regime.conditions: various mechanical testing conditions (e.g., tension, compression, hardness)

prior_attempts: extensive studies on the overall mechanical properties of HEAs, but not on individual elemental effects

prior attempts focused on overall mechanical properties
